source: NCERT Class XII, Themes in Indian History Part III, Ch. 11 (Rebels and the Raj: The Revolt of 1857).

sections.heading: 1. The Revolt of 1857 — Outbreak
points: The **Revolt of 1857** (the First War of Independence / the Great Rebellion / the Sepoy Mutiny) began at **Meerut (10 May 1857)** and spread across north/central India.
The immediate cause: the **greased cartridges** (rumoured to use cow and pig fat) for the new Enfield rifle — offending Hindu and Muslim sepoys; **Mangal Pandey (Barrackpore)** was an early rebel.
The rebels marched to **Delhi** and proclaimed the Mughal emperor **Bahadur Shah Zafar** as their symbolic leader.

sections.heading: 2. Causes of the Revolt
points: **Political:** annexations (Doctrine of Lapse — **Awadh annexed 1856**), loss of power of rulers.
**Economic:** heavy revenue, ruin of artisans, exploitation of peasants.
**Social/religious:** fear that the British aimed to destroy religion/convert to Christianity; reforms resented.
**Military:** sepoys' grievances (pay, promotion, the cartridges).

sections.heading: 3. Leaders and Centres
points: **Delhi** — Bahadur Shah Zafar (and General Bakht Khan).
**Kanpur** — **Nana Sahib** (and Tantia Tope).
**Lucknow (Awadh)** — **Begum Hazrat Mahal**.
**Jhansi** — **Rani Lakshmibai**.
**Bihar** — **Kunwar Singh**.
The revolt drew sepoys, peasants, artisans, and dispossessed rulers.

sections.heading: 4. Suppression and Consequences
points: The British suppressed the revolt with great force by **1858** (recapture of Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi).

**Consequences:** the **East India Company's rule ended**; India came under the **direct rule of the British Crown (Government of India Act, 1858)**; **Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858)** promised reforms.
The Mughal dynasty ended (Bahadur Shah Zafar exiled to Rangoon); a policy of caution towards Indian religion/customs followed.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: 1857 revolt began at Meerut (10 May 1857); trigger = greased cartridges; Mangal Pandey (Barrackpore).
Rebels proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar (Delhi) as leader.
Leaders: Nana Sahib (Kanpur), Begum Hazrat Mahal (Lucknow), Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Kunwar Singh (Bihar).
Doctrine of Lapse; Awadh annexed 1856 (a major cause).
Result: Company rule ended → British Crown rule (Act of 1858); Queen Victoria's Proclamation.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The revolt began at **Meerut** (10 May 1857); **Mangal Pandey** was at **Barrackpore**.
**Bahadur Shah Zafar (Delhi)** was the symbolic leader; **Begum Hazrat Mahal** led at **Lucknow**.
The revolt ended **Company rule** → India came under the **British Crown (1858)**.
**Awadh was annexed in 1856** (Doctrine of Lapse/misgovernance pretext).
